passages.text: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah was the ruler of Judah.
He heard the report from his officials.
He tore his clothes.
He put on sackcloth.
He entered the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֑יו וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And he sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz to tell him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah was in great distress.
Hezekiah sent messengers to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
He sent Eliakim, who managed the palace.
He sent Shebna, who was the scribe.
He sent the leading priests.
All of them wore sackcloth.
They went to Isaiah.
They spoke to Isaiah for Hezekiah.
They said, “Hezekiah says this.
Today is a day of trouble.
Today is a day of rebuke.
Today is a day of disgrace.
Children have come to the moment of birth.
But there is no strength to deliver them.”
passages.original: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ אֶלְיָקִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַבַּ֜יִת וְשֶׁבְנָ֣א הַסֹּפֵ֗ר וְאֵת֙ זִקְנֵ֣י הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים אֶל־ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא בֶּן־ אָמֽוֹץ׃ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם־ צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד־ מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh to defy the living God.
The Rabshakeh spoke many words against God.
Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all these words.
The LORD your God has already heard what the Rabshakeh said.
Perhaps the LORD your God will rebuke the Rabshakeh for these words.
Pray for the people who remain.
These people are the remnant that still survives.
passages.original: אוּלַ֡י יִשְׁמַע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת׀ כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֣י רַב־ שָׁקֵ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שְׁלָח֨וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֤וּר׀ אֲדֹנָיו֙ לְחָרֵף֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַ֔י וְהוֹכִ֙יחַ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ע יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְנָשָׂ֣אתָ תְפִלָּ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד הַשְּׁאֵרִ֖ית הַנִּמְצָאָֽה׃

passages.text: So the servants of King Hezekiah went to Isaiah, who replied, “Tell your master that this is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah had servants.
These servants went to Isaiah.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke to the servants.
Isaiah gave them a message for Hezekiah.
Isaiah said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD said, “Do not be afraid.”
The LORD spoke about the words Hezekiah heard.
The LORD said the servants of the king of Assyria spoke these words.
The servants of the king of Assyria blasphemed the LORD.
The LORD told Hezekiah not to fear these words.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל־ יְשַֽׁעַיָֽהוּ׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל־ אֲדֹֽנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־ תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֖וּר אֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke about the king of Assyria.
The LORD said, “I will act against him.
I will put a spirit in him.
He will hear a rumor.
He will return to his own land.
I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”
passages.original: הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֥ן בּוֹ֙ ר֔וּחַ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שְׁמוּעָ֖ה וְשָׁ֣ב לְאַרְצ֑וֹ וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was a high official of the king of Assyria.
The Rabshakeh heard news about the king of Assyria.
He heard that the king had left Lachish.
The Rabshakeh went back.
He found the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria was fighting against Libnah.
passages.original: וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת־ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל־ לִבְנָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י נָסַ֖ע מִלָּכִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Now Sennacherib had been warned about Tirhakah king of Cush: “Look, he has set out to fight against you.” So Sennacherib again sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying, “Give this message to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He heard news about Tirhakah.
Tirhakah was the king of Cush.
Sennacherib learned that Tirhakah had set out to fight against him.
Sennacherib returned from his previous position.
He sent messengers to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
The messengers brought a message for Hezekiah.
The message said: “Do not let your God deceive you.
You trust in your God.
Do not believe that Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע אֶל־ תִּרְהָ֤קָה מֶֽלֶך־ כּוּשׁ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֥ה יָצָ֖א לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם אִתָּ֑ךְ וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־ יַשִּׁאֲךָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בֹּטֵ֥חַ בּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries, devoting them to destruction. Will you then be spared?
passages.sermon:
The kings of Assyria are powerful rulers.
They attacked many countries.
They destroyed those countries completely.
You have heard about these things.
You know what the kings of Assyria did.
Do you think you will escape?
Will you be spared?
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה׀ אַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר לְכָל־ הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת לְהַֽחֲרִימָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּנָּצֵֽל׃

passages.text: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations—the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and of the people of Eden in Telassar?
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib spoke about the nations his fathers destroyed.
He asked a question about their gods.
He said, “Did the gods of those nations save them?”
He named the nations Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph.
He also named the people of Eden in Telassar.
Sennacherib said his fathers destroyed these nations.
He said their gods did not rescue them.
passages.original: הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שִׁחֲת֣וּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֶת־ גּוֹזָ֖ן וְאֶת־ חָרָ֑ן וְרֶ֥צֶף וּבְנֵי־ עֶ֖דֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּתְלַאשָּֽׂר׃

passages.text: Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’ ”
passages.sermon:
The kings of Assyria destroyed many nations.
They conquered Hamath.
They conquered Arpad.
They conquered Sepharvaim.
They conquered Hena.
They conquered Ivvah.
The kings of these cities are gone.
Where are the kings of Hamath?
Where are the kings of Arpad?
Where are the kings of Sepharvaim?
Where are the kings of Hena?
Where are the kings of Ivvah?
passages.original: אַיּ֤וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־ חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם הֵנַ֖ע וְעִוָּֽה׃

passages.text: So Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, read it, and went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah received a letter from the messengers.
Hezekiah took the letter from their hand.
Hezekiah read the letter.
Hezekiah went up to the house of the LORD.
Hezekiah spread the letter out before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת־ הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑ם וַיַּ֙עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD: “O LORD, God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah prayed before the LORD.
Hezekiah spoke to the LORD.
Hezekiah said, “LORD, God of Israel, you sit above the cherubim.
You alone are God.
You rule over all the kingdoms of the earth.
You made the heavens.
You made the earth.”
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. Listen to the words that Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah spoke to the LORD, the God of Israel.
Hezekiah said, “LORD, incline Your ear and hear.
LORD, open Your eyes and see.
LORD, listen to the words of Sennacherib.
Sennacherib has sent these words to insult the living God.”
passages.original: הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה׀ אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖יךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁלָח֔וֹ לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃

passages.text: Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste these nations and their lands.
passages.sermon: The kings of Assyria destroyed many nations.\r\nThe kings of Assyria ruined their lands.\r\nO LORD, this is true.
passages.original: אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם וְאֶת־ אַרְצָֽם׃

passages.text: They have cast their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods, but only wood and stone—the work of human hands.
passages.sermon:
The kings of Assyria took the gods of the nations.
They threw these gods into the fire.
These gods were not real gods.
They were only wood and stone.
People made them with their own hands.
The kings of Assyria destroyed them.
passages.original: וְנָתְנ֥וּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־ מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־ אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃

passages.text: And now, O LORD our God, please save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah said, "Now, LORD our God, save us from his hand."
Hezekiah asked God to rescue them from the king of Assyria.
Hezekiah wanted all the kingdoms of the earth to know something.
He wanted them to know that the LORD alone is God.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א מִיָּד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah was the son of Amoz.
Isaiah sent a message to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Isaiah spoke for the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, “I have heard your prayer.”
Hezekiah prayed about Sennacherib.
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִתְפַּלַּ֧לְתָּ אֵלַ֛י אֶל־ סַנְחֵרִ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֖וּר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: This is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: ‘The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke a word against Sennacherib, king of Assyria.
The LORD said this word about him.
The Virgin Daughter of Zion is Jerusalem.
The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you.
The Virgin Daughter of Zion mocks you.
The Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
She does this behind you.
passages.original: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־ צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib is the king of Assyria.
He taunted and blasphemed someone.
He raised his voice against someone.
He lifted his eyes in pride against someone.
He did these things against the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: אֶת־ מִ֤י חֵרַ֙פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־ מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָ קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ עַל־ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the remote peaks of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses. I have reached its farthest outposts, the densest of its forests.
passages.sermon:
You have taunted the Lord through your servants.
You said these things with pride.
You said, “I have many chariots.
I went up to the high mountains.
I reached the far peaks of Lebanon.
I cut down the tallest cedar trees there.
I took the best cypress trees.
I went to the farthest places.
I entered the thickest forests.”
passages.original: בְּיַ֣ד מַלְאָכֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ׀ אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֶכֶב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְח֣וֹר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָב֙וֹאָה֙ מְל֣וֹן קִצֹּ֔ה יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is the king of Assyria.  
The king of Assyria boasts about his power.  
He says, "I have dug wells."  
He says, "I have drunk water from foreign lands."  
He says, "I have dried up all the streams of Egypt with the soles of my feet."
passages.original: אֲנִ֣י קַ֔רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֖יתִי מַ֣יִם זָרִ֑ים וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־ פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the proud king.
God asks a question.
God says, “Have you not heard?”
God explains His actions.
God says, “Long ago I decided this.”
God says, “In ancient times I planned it.”
God says, “Now I have made it happen.”
God says, “You destroy strong cities.”
God says, “You turn them into heaps of ruins.”
passages.original: הֲלֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי לְמִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִֽיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵיאתִ֗יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לַהְשׁ֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, are dismayed and ashamed. They are like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.
passages.sermon:
The people who live there have no strength.
They feel afraid.
They feel ashamed.
They are like grass in a field.
They are like young green plants.
They are like grass that grows on rooftops.
The sun burns them before they grow tall.
passages.original: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־ יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וַיֵּבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃

passages.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks here.
God knows everything about you.
God knows when you sit down.
God knows when you go out.
God knows when you come in.
God knows when you rage against Him.
passages.original: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Because your rage and arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the enemy of Judah.
You have raged against Me.
You have shown arrogance toward Me.
Your rage and arrogance have reached My ears.
I will act against you.
I will put My hook in your nose.
I will put My bit in your mouth.
I will force you to return.
You will go back the way you came.
passages.original: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣בֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to King Hezekiah.
God gave a sign to Hezekiah.
This sign would show God's promise.
In the first year, you will eat what grows by itself.
You will not plant or harvest in the first year.
In the second year, you will eat what grows from the same plants.
You will not plant or harvest in the second year either.
In the third year, you will plant seeds.
You will harvest what you plant in the third year.
You will plant vineyards in the third year.
You will eat the fruit from your vineyards in the third year.
passages.original: וְזֶה־ לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית סָחִ֑ישׁ וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאִכְל֥וּ פִרְיָֽם׃

passages.text: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.
passages.sermon: The house of Judah has a remnant that survives.\r\nThis remnant will take root below.\r\nThis remnant will bear fruit above.
passages.original: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־ יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃

passages.text: For a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
passages.sermon:
A remnant will go out from Jerusalem.
Survivors will come from Mount Zion.
The LORD of Hosts is zealous.
The LORD of Hosts will do this.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥הֳ֖ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ זֹּֽאת׃ס

passages.text: So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke about the king of Assyria.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said these words.
The king of Assyria will not enter this city.
He will not shoot an arrow into this city.
He will not come before this city with a shield.
He will not build a siege ramp against this city.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבֹא֙ אֶל־ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־ יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־ יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־ יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עָלֶ֖יהָ סֹלְלָֽה׃

passages.text: He will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city,’ declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD refers to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria came by a certain way.
He will return by that same way.
He will not enter this city.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ יָבֹ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָבֹ֖א נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises to defend this city.
The LORD will save this city.
The LORD acts for His own sake.
The LORD acts for the sake of His servant David.
passages.original: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י אֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃

passages.text: And that very night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD is a messenger sent by God.
That night, the angel of the LORD went out.
He entered the camp of the Assyrians.
He struck down 185,000 men in the camp.
In the morning, the people got up.
They saw all the dead bodies.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֵּצֵ֣א׀ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּךְ֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃

passages.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He broke camp.
He left the area.
He returned to Nineveh.
He stayed in Nineveh.
passages.original: וַיִּסַּ֣ע וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖שָׁב סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּנִֽינְוֵֽה׃

passages.text: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
One day, Sennacherib worshiped in the temple of his god Nisroch.
His sons were Adrammelech and Sharezer.
Adrammelech and Sharezer killed Sennacherib with a sword.
Adrammelech and Sharezer escaped to the land of Ararat.
Esar-haddon was Sennacherib’s son.
Esar-haddon became king after Sennacherib.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶרָָ֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־ חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
